title: Can Humanity Become a New Species?
logline: When technology begins to shape evolution, the definition of 'human' may change forever.
thesis: Human evolution is no longer driven only by nature; technology is creating new forces of divergence.

sentences.text: Humans carry a small but measurable percentage of Neanderthal DNA from encounters tens of thousands of years ago.
But what if our species could split again — this time, driven by technology rather than ice and isolation?
In classical biology, a species is a group of organisms that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring.
The definition works well for well-isolated populations but blurs at the edges.
Modern humans and Neanderthals interbred, leaving a small genetic legacy in non-African populations today.

sections.heading: Technology as a new evolutionary force

sentences.text: CRISPR and other gene-editing tools could alter the human germline within a generation.
If heritable changes are introduced and propagate through a population, the result may be a new lineage.
